mainTopic: Did בית שמאי practice their view on צרת הבת? The story of רבי דוסא בן הרכינס and the three הלכות of חגי הנביא
overview: The גמרא finishes its proofs that בית שמאי really acted on their view that the צרה of a daughter may marry the brothers, and concludes that they did. It then tells the full story behind one of those proofs. רבי יהושע, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה and רבי עקיבא visit the elderly, nearly blind רבי דוסא בן הרכינס, who welcomes each one warmly. When they ask about צרת הבת, he rules like בית הלל and explains that the ruling quoted as 'בן הרכינס' came from his brother יונתן, a student of שמאי. He swears that חגי הנביא taught three הלכות: צרת הבת is forbidden, עמון ומואב give מעשר עני in שביעית, and גרים are accepted from the קרדויים and תרמודים. רבי עקיבא then holds his ground against יונתן and answers his insult with humility. The גמרא explains חגי's second and third הלכות and settles a challenge about the קרדויים. Finally it brings רבי יוחנן's view that גרים are not accepted from the תרמודים and begins questioning it from a משנה about stains from רקם. That discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the testimony about children of rival wives
steps.stepSummary: The last words of a quoted testimony: 'As for the children of צרות, I testify to you.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As for children of rival wives, I testify to you.
steps.whatsHappening: This line closes a quote that started earlier. The speaker testifies that children born to צרות were treated as fully kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If children of צרות married under בית שמאי's view were accepted as fit, then בית שמאי really did act on their opinion. This line finishes that proof.

phrases.english: Children of rival wives — I testify to you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a proof begun before this text, that בית שמאי acted on their view.
steps.raayaObject: That בית שמאי actually put their ruling about צרות into practice.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Testimony that children of צרות were accepted as fully fit.

steps.title: Another proof from the days of רבי דוסא בן הרכינס
steps.stepSummary: In the days of רבי דוסא בן הרכינס, a daughter's rival wife was allowed to the brothers, so בית שמאי did act on their view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: In the days of רבי דוסא בן הרכינס, the rival wife of a daughter was permitted to the brothers. Learn from this that they acted on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more source showing that בית שמאי's ruling was really practiced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Permitting a צרת הבת to the brothers is בית שמאי's view. If it was actually permitted in a real period of history, then their view was carried out in practice and not just discussed.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: introduces a source used as proof
The rival wife of a daughter (the co-wife of a man's daughter)
They acted (put the ruling into practice)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
In the days of Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas
the rival wife of a daughter was permitted to the brothers.
phrases.notes: 'The brothers' are the brothers of the husband who died, who could marry her through יבום.

phrases.english: Learn from this: they acted on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another proof to the same question.
steps.raayaObject: That בית שמאי acted on their view.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A report that in רבי דוסא בן הרכינס's time a צרת הבת was permitted to the brothers.

steps.title: Conclusion: בית שמאי did act on their view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the proofs: yes, learn from this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up and accepts the proofs: בית שמאי really did practice their ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was whether בית שמאי only held their view in theory or also acted on it. With these sources, the גמרא decides that they acted on it.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it (the point is proven)

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי did not just hold their view about צרת הבת in theory. It was actually practiced.

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proofs just brought.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: בית שמאי did put their ruling about צרות into practice.

steps.title: The full story: the חכמים were troubled by רבי דוסא's ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the full story. In רבי דוסא's days a צרת הבת was permitted, and the חכמים were troubled because he was a great חכם whose eyes were too weak to come to the בית המדרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: In the days of רבי דוסא בן הרכינס they permitted the rival wife of a daughter to the brothers. This was hard for the חכמים, because he was a great חכם, and his eyes had grown too dim for him to come to the בית המדרש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now tells the whole story behind the short line it just quoted. This opens a longer story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling was troubling because it came from someone as great as רבי דוסא, so it carried real weight. They could not simply discuss it with him in the בית המדרש, because he was old and could no longer see well enough to come.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The thing itself': the גמרא returns to quote a source in full

phrases.english: The matter itself:
In the days of Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas
they permitted the rival wife of a daughter to the brothers,
and the matter was difficult for the Sages,
because he was a great Sage,
and his eyes had grown dim,
so he could not come to the study hall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the short quote from step 2 into its full story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי דוסא's time a צרת הבת was permitted, and this troubled the חכמים because of his great stature.

steps.title: Three great חכמים go to visit רבי דוסא
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask who will go speak with him. רבי יהושע volunteers, followed by רבי אלעזר בן עזריה and רבי עקיבא. They arrive, the maidservant announces them, and he lets them in.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Who will go and let him know? רבי יהושע said: I will go. And who after him? רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. And who after him? רבי עקיבא. They went and stood at the entrance of his house. His maidservant went in and said to him: רבי, the חכמים of Israel have come to you. He said to her: Let them come in. And they came in.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. A group of leading חכמים goes to רבי דוסא's home to discuss the ruling with him. This sets up the conversation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since he could not come to them, they went to him. Sending such important people, one after another, shows how seriously they treated both the question and רבי דוסא.

phrases.english: They said: And who will go and inform him?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: אֲנִי אֵלֵךְ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to them: I will go.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחֲרָיו מִי — רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה.
phrases.english: And who after him? Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.
And who after him? Rabbi Akiva.
They went and stood at the entrance of his house.
His maidservant went in and said to him:
Rabbi, the Sages of Israel are coming to you.
He said to her: Let them enter. And they entered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: the חכמים respond to the problem by visiting רבי דוסא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה and רבי עקיבא go to רבי דוסא's home, and he welcomes them in.

steps.title: רבי דוסא welcomes רבי יהושע and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסא seats רבי יהושע on a golden bed. When he hears that רבי אלעזר בן עזריה is the son of his old friend עזריה, he quotes a פסוק in his praise and seats him too.
steps.simpleTranslation: He grabbed רבי יהושע and sat him on a golden bed. רבי יהושע said: 'רבי, tell your other student to sit too.' He asked, 'Who is it?' 'רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.' He said, 'Our friend עזריה has a son?' He recited about him: 'I have been young and now am old, yet I have not seen the righteous forsaken, nor his children begging bread.' Then he grabbed him and sat him on a golden bed.
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on. רבי דוסא greets his guests one at a time, starting with רבי יהושע and then רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע calls each colleague 'your student' to show respect to the elderly רבי דוסא. Because רבי דוסא had stayed home for so long, he had not even heard that his friend עזריה had a son who became a חכם. The פסוק he quotes praises the fact that a צדיק's child turned out great.

keyTerms.meaning: A bed (couch) of gold, a sign of honor and wealth
Your student, said here as a respectful way of speaking

phrases.english: He grabbed Rabbi Yehoshua,
and sat him on a bed of gold.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: רַבִּי, אֱמוֹר לְתַלְמִידְךָ אַחֵר וְיֵשֵׁב.
phrases.english: He said to him: Rabbi, tell your other student to sit as well.
phrases.notes: רבי יהושע calls his colleague 'your student' out of respect for רבי דוסא. He isn't really his student.

phrases.english: He said to him: Who is it?
Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: וְיֵשׁ לוֹ בֵּן לַעֲזַרְיָה חֲבֵירֵנוּ?
phrases.english: He said: Does our friend Azarya have a son?
He recited this verse about him:
"I have been young, and now am old,
yet I have not seen the righteous forsaken,
nor his children begging bread."

phrases.aramaic: תְּפָסוֹ וְהוֹשִׁיבוֹ עַל מִטָּה שֶׁל זָהָב.
phrases.english: He grabbed him and sat him on a bed of gold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story right after רבי דוסא lets the visitors in.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי דוסא honors רבי יהושע and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, praising the latter with a פסוק.

steps.title: רבי דוסא welcomes רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע introduces רבי עקיבא. רבי דוסא recognizes his world-famous name and blesses him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said: 'רבי, tell your other student to sit.' He asked, 'Who is it?' 'עקיבא בן יוסף.' He said: 'You are עקיבא בן יוסף, whose name is known from one end of the world to the other? Sit, my son, sit. May there be many more like you in Israel.'
steps.whatsHappening: The third guest, רבי עקיבא, is introduced. Even רבי דוסא, who stayed home, had heard of him, and he gives him a warm blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This finishes the welcome before the real business begins. It shows how great רבי עקיבא's reputation already was, since even someone cut off from the בית המדרש knew his name.

keyTerms.meaning: Sit, my son, a warm and fatherly greeting
From one end of the world to the other

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: רַבִּי, אֱמוֹר לְתַלְמִידְךָ אַחֵר וְיֵשֵׁב.
phrases.english: He said to him: Rabbi, tell your other student to sit as well.
He said to him: And who is it?
Akiva ben Yosef.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: אַתָּה הוּא עֲקִיבָא בֶּן יוֹסֵף
phrases.english: He said to him: You are Akiva ben Yosef,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁשִּׁמְךָ הוֹלֵךְ מִסּוֹף הָעוֹלָם וְעַד סוֹפוֹ?!
phrases.english: whose name has spread from one end of the world to the other?!
Sit, my son, sit.
May there be many like you in Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: רַבִּי, אֱמוֹר לְתַלְמִידְךָ אַחֵר וְיֵשֵׁב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as the last step, now for the third guest.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי דוסא honors and blesses רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: The visitors ask about צרת הבת
steps.stepSummary: After talking about other הלכות, the חכמים finally reach the real reason for their visit and ask about צרת הבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: They began talking around him with various הלכות until they reached צרת הבת. They asked him: 'What is the law of צרת הבת?'
steps.whatsHappening: The guests politely ease into the topic and then ask the question they came for. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Out of respect they don't jump straight to the touchy issue. They want to find out whether the report that צרת הבת was allowed in his days really reflects his own opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: The rival wife (co-wife) of a daughter, in the case of יבום
What is it? What is the law?

phrases.english: They began to circle around him with various laws,
until they reached the rival wife of a daughter.
They said to him: What is the law of the rival wife of a daughter?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the greetings, the visitors turn to the purpose of the visit described in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the הלכה regarding צרת הבת, and what is רבי דוסא's own view?

steps.title: רבי דוסא rules like בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסא says צרת הבת is a מחלוקת between בית שמאי and בית הלל, and the הלכה follows בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: 'It is a מחלוקת between בית שמאי and בית הלל.' They asked: 'Whose opinion is the הלכה?' He said: 'The הלכה follows בית הלל.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי דוסא answers the question. He rules like בית הלל, who forbid צרת הבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is surprising, because the report was that in his days צרת הבת was allowed, which is בית שמאי's view. His clear answer sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The two great schools of חכמים
The law follows the opinion of

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן: מַחְלוֹקֶת בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל.
phrases.english: He said to them: It is a dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel.
They asked: Whose words does the law follow?
He said to them: The law follows Beit Hillel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: מַחְלוֹקֶת בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The הלכה follows בית הלל, so צרת הבת is forbidden.

steps.title: But a ruling like בית שמאי was quoted in your name
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים point out that people quoted him as ruling like בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: 'But didn't they say in your name that the הלכה follows בית שמאי?'
steps.whatsHappening: The visitors challenge his answer with the report they had heard, which is why they came in the first place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His ruling now contradicts the quote attributed to him. The challenge pushes him to explain where that quote really came from.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that, opening a challenge

phrases.english: They said to him: But didn't they say in your name
that the law follows Beit Shammai!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling just given in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי דוסא's statement that the הלכה follows בית הלל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ruling like בית שמאי was reported in his name, which contradicts what he just said.

steps.title: It was my brother יונתן, not me
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסא asks whether they heard the name 'דוסא' or only 'בן הרכינס.' When they say only 'בן הרכינס,' he explains that his sharp younger brother יונתן, a student of שמאי, is the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: 'Did you hear "דוסא," or did you hear "בן הרכינס"?' They said: 'By your life, רבי, we just heard "בן הרכינס."' He said: 'I have a younger brother, a firstborn of the שטן, named יונתן, and he is one of the students of שמאי.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי דוסא resolves the contradiction. The quote really came from his brother, who has the same family name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both brothers could be called 'בן הרכינס,' so a quote with only that name could belong to either one. Since יונתן was a student of שמאי, the ruling like בית שמאי came from him, and רבי דוסא's own view is like בית הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: By the life of the רבי, a respectful oath
Firstborn of the שטן, meaning extremely sharp and bold

steps.whatToRemember: רבי דוסא himself held like בית הלל. The ruling like בית שמאי quoted as 'בן הרכינס' came from his brother יונתן, a student of שמאי.
steps.confusionAlert: 'בן הרכינס' is a family name shared by both brothers. That is why a quote with only that name was mistakenly linked to רבי דוסא.

phrases.english: He said to them: Did you hear "Dosa,"
or did you hear "ben Harkinas"?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לוֹ: חַיֵּי רַבִּי, סְתָם שָׁמַעְנוּ.
phrases.english: They said to him: By your life, Rabbi, we heard it plainly.
phrases.notes: 'Plainly' means they only heard 'ben Harkinas,' with no first name attached.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: אָח קָטָן יֵשׁ לִי,
phrases.english: He said to them: I have a younger brother,
he is a firstborn of the Satan,
phrases.notes: He means his brother is extremely sharp and bold in argument.

phrases.english: and his name is Yonatan,
and he is one of the students of Shammai.

steps.triggerLanguage: דּוֹסָא שְׁמַעְתֶּם, אוֹ בֶּן הַרְכִּינָס שְׁמַעְתֶּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 10 by showing the quote came from someone else.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Misattribution: the name in the report belongs to a different person
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling like בית שמאי quoted as 'ben Harkinas' was רבי דוסא's own view.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling came from his brother יונתן, a student of שמאי. רבי דוסא himself rules like בית הלל.

steps.title: Warning about יונתן's 300 arguments
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסא warns the חכמים that his brother יונתן will try to overwhelm them with 300 arguments that צרת הבת is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Be careful that he doesn't crush you with הלכות, because he has 300 arguments that צרת הבת is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי דוסא is still speaking. He warns the חכמים about his brother יונתן before they go to meet him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יונתן is the one who rules like בית שמאי, so he permits צרת הבת. רבי דוסא warns that יונתן is so sharp he has 300 proofs for his view. This sets up the next step, where רבי דוסא gives a powerful source for the opposite view.

phrases.english: And be careful that he does not crush you with הלכות,
phrases.notes: "He" is יונתן, רבי דוסא's younger brother from the step before.

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ עִמּוֹ שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת תְּשׁוּבוֹת
phrases.english: because he has with him three hundred arguments
regarding צרת הבת, that she is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי דוסא's explanation about his brother יונתן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יונתן has 300 arguments for permitting צרת הבת, so the חכמים must be careful.

steps.title: Testimony from חגי הנביא
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסא swears that חגי הנביא sat on this seat and taught three הלכות. The first is that צרת הבת is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But I call heaven and earth as witnesses that חגי הנביא sat on this seat and said three things: צרת הבת is forbidden; עמון and מואב give מעשר עני in the שביעית year; and we accept גרים from the קרדויין and the תרמודים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי דוסא backs up his ruling like בית הלל with a tradition going back to חגי הנביא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if יונתן has 300 arguments, a ruling from a נביא carries more weight. חגי ruled צרת הבת is forbidden, which matches בית הלל. The other two הלכות come along because they are part of the same tradition.

keyTerms.meaning: a mortar; here, a seat he sat on
the tithe given to the poor

steps.whyThisMatters: It firmly ties the ruling that צרת הבת is forbidden to a tradition from the time of the נביאים.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מֵעִיד אֲנִי עָלַי שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ,
phrases.english: But I call heaven and earth as witnesses for me,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁעַל מְדוֹכָה זוֹ יָשַׁב חַגַּי הַנָּבִיא,
phrases.english: that on this mortar sat חגי the prophet,
and said three things:
צרת הבת is forbidden,

phrases.aramaic: עַמּוֹן וּמוֹאָב מְעַשְּׂרִין מַעְשַׂר עָנִי בַּשְּׁבִיעִית,
phrases.english: Ammon and Moab separate the poor man's tithe in the seventh year,
and we accept converts
from the Karduyin and from the Tarmodim.
phrases.notes: These are names of non-Jewish peoples.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל מֵעִיד אֲנִי עָלַי שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the worry about יונתן's 300 arguments with a source from a נביא.
steps.raayaObject: The הלכה follows בית הלל: צרת הבת is forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A tradition from חגי הנביא, who sat on this mortar.

steps.title: The חכמים leave and רבי עקיבא faces יונתן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the חכמים came in through one door but left through three to find יונתן. רבי עקיבא met him and answered all his challenges.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: when they came in, they came through one door. When they left, they left through three doors. רבי עקיבא met him. He challenged him, and רבי עקיבא held his ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves forward. The חכמים split up to find יונתן, and רבי עקיבא is the one who meets him and debates him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving through three doors shows they spread out to look for יונתן. Even with his 300 arguments, יונתן could not defeat רבי עקיבא. This sets up the conversation in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: he stood up to him, held his ground

phrases.english: It was taught: when they entered, they entered through one doorway,
when they left, they left through three doorways.
Rabbi עקיבא ran into him,
phrases.notes: "Him" is יונתן, the brother they went looking for.

phrases.english: he challenged him, and he held his ground.
phrases.notes: יונתן threw his questions at רבי עקיבא, and רבי עקיבא answered every one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The warning about יונתן is now put to the test in a real debate.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא withstood all of יונתן's challenges.

steps.title: יונתן's remark to רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: יונתן asks if this is the famous עקיבא and says that, despite his fame, he hasn't even reached the level of cattle herders.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Are you עקיבא, whose name goes from one end of the world to the other? Fortunate are you that you earned a name, and yet you have not reached the level of cattle herders.
steps.whatsHappening: יונתן reacts to the debate with a sharp, belittling comment about רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יונתן admits that רבי עקיבא is famous, but he mocks him as being below even simple, unlearned cattle herders. This sets up רבי עקיבא's humble reply.

phrases.english: He said to him: Are you עקיבא

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁשִּׁמְךָ הוֹלֵךְ מִסּוֹף הָעוֹלָם וְעַד סוֹפוֹ?
phrases.english: whose name goes from one end of the world to the other?
Fortunate are you that you have earned a name,
and yet you have not reached the level of cattle herders.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: יונתן reacts after failing to defeat רבי עקיבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יונתן belittles רבי עקיבא as not yet on the level of cattle herders.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's humble reply
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers that he has not even reached the level of shepherds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: And not even the level of shepherds.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא does not fight back. He humbly agrees and lowers himself even more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Shepherds were considered even lower than cattle herders. So instead of defending his honor, רבי עקיבא says he is lower still. This shows his great humility.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי דוסא's ruling like בית הלל, that צרת הבת is forbidden, rests on a tradition from חגי הנביא. רבי עקיבא withstood יונתן's challenges and answered his insult with humility.

phrases.english: Rabbi עקיבא said to him:
And not even shepherds.
phrases.notes: He means: I haven't even reached the level of shepherds.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: וַאֲפִילּוּ לְרוֹעֵי צֹאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds directly to יונתן's remark.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: יונתן's implied challenge to רבי עקיבא's greatness.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי עקיבא humbly says he hasn't even reached the level of shepherds.

steps.title: חגי's second הלכה: עמון ומואב give מעשר עני in שביעית
steps.stepSummary: The second הלכה of חגי הנביא: in the lands of עמון ומואב, people separate מעשר עני during the שביעית year.
steps.simpleTranslation: עמון ומואב separate מעשר עני in the שביעית year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second of the three הלכות that רבי דוסא said חגי הנביא taught. In the lands of עמון ומואב, people separate מעשר עני even in the שביעית year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, the land is not farmed in ארץ ישראל during שביעית, so no מעשרות are taken. Here חגי rules that in עמון ומואב the land is farmed, and the tithe given is מעשר עני. The next step explains why.

keyTerms.meaning: The lands of Ammon and Moab, east of the ירדן
The poor man's tithe, given to the poor in certain years
The seventh year, when the land of ארץ ישראל rests

phrases.english: Ammon and Moab
phrases.notes: This is the second of the three הלכות of חגי that רבי דוסא swore by.

phrases.english: tithe the poor man's tithe in the Sabbatical Year.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַמּוֹן וּמוֹאָב מְעַשְּׂרִין מַעְשַׂר עָנִי בַּשְּׁבִיעִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of three הלכות of חגי begun in step 13, after the story of רבי עקיבא and יונתן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In עמון ומואב, people separate מעשר עני during שביעית.

steps.title: Why עמון ומואב are farmed and tithed in שביעית
steps.stepSummary: The first holiness of the land, from עולי מצרים, was only temporary. עולי בבל did not reconquer these areas and deliberately left them unholy so the poor could be supported in שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Master said: Many cities were conquered by those who came up from Egypt but were not conquered by those who came up from Babylonia. The first holiness sanctified the land only for its time, not for the future. And they left those places aside so that the poor could rely on them in the Sabbatical Year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the source behind חגי's ruling. The holiness that עולי מצרים gave these lands ended, and עולי בבל chose not to make them holy again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולי מצרים made these lands holy, but that holiness lasted only for its own time. עולי בבל did not conquer them again, so they had no שביעית holiness. They left them that way on purpose so these lands would be farmed in שביעית, and the מעשר עני from them would feed the poor.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who came up from Egypt, the first entry into the land
Those who came back from Babylonia after the first exile
The first holiness of ארץ ישראל

steps.confusionAlert: The holiness these places had from עולי מצרים did not last. עולי בבל did not conquer them again. Beyond that, they chose to leave them without holiness (וְהִנִּיחוּם) so the poor could rely on them in שביעית.

phrases.english: As the Master said:
Many cities were conquered by those who came up from Egypt
and were not conquered by those who came up from Babylonia,
and the first sanctification
sanctified for its time,
and did not sanctify for the future to come.
And they left them aside,
phrases.notes: "They" means עולי בבל, who chose not to make these places holy again.

phrases.english: so that the poor could rely on them in the Sabbatical Year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source and reasoning for the ruling in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that עמון ומואב give מעשר עני in שביעית.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A teaching of מר: the first holiness was temporary, and עולי בבל left these cities unholy to support the poor.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the idea that the holiness of the land from עולי מצרים did not last, which comes up in many places about שביעית and מעשרות.

steps.title: חגי's third הלכה: גרים are accepted from the קרדויים and תרמודים
steps.stepSummary: The third הלכה of חגי: we accept גרים from the קרדויים and the תרמודים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we accept גרים from the קרדויים and the תרמודים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the third הלכה of חגי. גרים may be accepted from two nations, the קרדויים and the תרמודים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might have thought these nations are too mixed or problematic to accept גרים from. חגי rules that we do accept them. This ruling sets up the challenge in the next step.

phrases.english: And we accept converts
from the Karduyim and the Tarmodim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the third and final הלכה of חגי after the second was explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We accept גרים from the קרדויים and the תרמודים.

steps.title: A ברייתא says not to accept גרים from the קרדויים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges חגי's ruling: רמי בר יחזקאל taught that we do NOT accept גרים from the קרדויים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so?! But didn't רמי בר יחזקאל teach: We do not accept גרים from the קרדויים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question against חגי's third הלכה. A ברייתא from רמי בר יחזקאל says the exact opposite about the קרדויים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חגי said we accept גרים from the קרדויים. רמי בר יחזקאל's ברייתא says we do not. These are two sources in direct conflict.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? (a sign of a challenge)
But didn't he teach (bringing a ברייתא against)

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But didn't Rami bar Yechezkel teach:
We do not accept converts from the Karduyim!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי וְהָא תָּנֵי רָמֵי בַּר יְחֶזְקֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: חגי's ruling that we accept גרים from the קרדויים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רמי בר יחזקאל's ברייתא directly forbids accepting גרים from the קרדויים.

steps.title: רב אשי: the ברייתא actually said קרתויים
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that רמי בר יחזקאל's ברייתא said קרתויים, a different group, not קרדויים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: "קרתויים" was stated. As people say: קרתויים are unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי solves the contradiction. He says the correct wording of the ברייתא is קרתויים, with a ת, not קרדויים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the ברייתא is read as קרתויים, it is talking about a different nation, so there is no conflict with חגי. רב אשי backs this up with a popular saying that קרתויים are unfit.

keyTerms.meaning: The Kartuyim, a different group from the קרדויים

steps.confusionAlert: קרדויים (with ד) and קרתויים (with ת) look and sound almost the same, but רב אשי treats them as two different nations.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
"Kartuyim" was stated.
phrases.notes: He means רמי בר יחזקאל really said קרתויים, with a ת, not קרדויים.

phrases.english: As people say:
Kartuyim are unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the challenging source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא forbids גרים from the קרדויים, against חגי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about the קרתויים, a different group, so חגי's ruling about קרדויים stands.

steps.title: Second version: maybe קרתויים and קרדויים are the same people
steps.stepSummary: In a second version, רמי בר יחזקאל's ברייתא already says קרתויים, and the challenge is that קרתויים might be the same as קרדויים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there are those who say: רמי בר יחזקאל taught: We do not accept גרים from the קרתויים. What, is it not that קרתויים are the same as קרדויים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another version of the same discussion. Here the ברייתא already says קרתויים, and the challenge is that this name may just be another way of saying קרדויים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version nobody disputes the wording of the ברייתא. The question is whether the two names mean the same nation. If they do, the ברייתא still contradicts חגי.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who say (introducing another version)
What, is it not that (suggesting an understanding)

phrases.english: And there are those who say:
Rami bar Yechezkel taught:
We do not accept converts from the Kartuyim.
What, is it not that
Kartuyim are the same as Karduyim!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי תָּנֵי רָמֵי בַּר יְחֶזְקֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates the challenge of step 20 in a different version, where the wording of the ברייתא is already קרתויים.
steps.kashyaTarget: חגי's ruling that we accept גרים from the קרדויים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If קרתויים is just another name for קרדויים, the ברייתא forbids what חגי permitted.

steps.title: רב אשי: קרתויים and קרדויים are two separate groups
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that קרתויים and קרדויים are different nations, as the saying goes, "קרתויים are unfit."
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: No, קרתויים are separate and קרדויים are separate, as people say: קרתויים are unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי rejects the idea that the two names mean the same nation. So the ברייתא and חגי do not argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both versions, רב אשי's answer rests on the same idea: the forbidden group is the קרתויים. Here he says it by separating the two names instead of fixing the wording. חגי's ruling permitting גרים from the קרדויים stands.
steps.whatToRemember: חגי taught three הלכות: צרת הבת is forbidden; עמון ומואב give מעשר עני in שביעית, because עולי בבל left those lands unholy to help the poor; and we accept גרים from the קרדויים and תרמודים. The ברייתא that forbids גרים is talking about the קרתויים, a different group.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: No,
Kartuyim are separate and Karduyim are separate,
as people say:
Kartuyim are unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי לָא קַרְתּוֹיֵי לְחוֹד וְקַרְדּוֹיֵי לְחוֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of the second version in step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing two groups with similar names
steps.terutzHavaAmina: קרתויים and קרדויים are the same nation, so the ברייתא contradicts חגי.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are two separate nations; only the קרתויים are unfit, so חגי's ruling stands.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן and the סביא reject גרים from the תרמודים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and the סביא both rule that we do not accept גרים from the תרמודים, the opposite of חגי's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן and the Elders both say: we do not accept converts from the תרמודים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new opinion that disagrees with חגי. רבי יוחנן and the סביא say we do NOT accept גרים from the תרמודים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חגי said we DO accept גרים from both the קרדויים and the תרמודים. The גמרא already defended the קרדויים part, but on the תרמודים there is now a real disagreement. This opinion becomes the target of the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: The Elders, a group of older sages
The people of תרמוד, a place on the edge of the Jewish world

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and the Elders
who both say:
We do not accept converts from the Tarmodim.
phrases.notes: This is the opposite of what חגי said back in step 19.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the קרדויים discussion to the תרמודים part of חגי's ruling and brings an opposing opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוחנן and the סביא, גרים are not accepted from the תרמודים.

steps.title: Did רבי יוחנן really say this? A משנה about stains from רקם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether רבי יוחנן really held this, quoting a משנה: bloodstains from רקם are טהור, but רבי יהודה calls them טמא because the people there are 'גרים וטועים'. It ends with 'והוינן בה', opening a discussion that continues next.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי יוחנן really say this? But we learned in a משנה: all bloodstains that come from רקם are pure. רבי יהודה says they are impure, because those people are converts who go astray. Stains from among the gentiles are pure. And we discussed this משנה:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether רבי יוחנן truly said we don't accept גרים from the תרמודים, and quotes a משנה about bloodstains from the town of רקם. The final words 'והוינן בה' are a setup: the גמרא is about to bring an earlier discussion of this משנה, which will show the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says stains from רקם are טהור, since we assume they came from non-Jewish women. רבי יהודה disagrees and calls them טמא, because people there are גרים who have strayed from keeping the Torah. The full force of the challenge to רבי יוחנן only becomes clear in the discussion that comes right after 'והוינן בה'.

keyTerms.meaning: And did he really say? (a challenge opener)
But didn't we learn in a משנה?
Bloodstains found on clothing that might be נדה blood
A town on the border of ארץ ישראל
Converts who go astray from keeping the Torah
And we discussed it (introduces an earlier discussion)

steps.confusionAlert: This משנה is about טומאה of bloodstains, not about accepting גרים. The גמרא brings it only because it describes the people of רקם, and the link to רבי יוחנן will come in the discussion that follows.

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Yochanan really say this?
But didn't we learn in a mishnah:
All the bloodstains
that come from Rekem
are pure.
And Rabbi Yehuda declares them impure,
because they are converts who go astray.
From among the gentiles, they are pure.
And we discussed it:

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָכִי? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the opinion of רבי יוחנן brought in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that גרים are not accepted from the תרמודים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The גמרא brings a משנה about the people of רקם, described by רבי יהודה as 'גרים וטועים'. The discussion of this משנה that follows 'והוינן בה' will show how it conflicts with רבי יוחנן's ruling.
